reason: Ranked first the store extraction reorder and counter scheduling: both target the hot path with small, localized changes and leave packing and arithmetic intact. A-transpose and scratch-lifetime changes next address the existing 128 KiB per-call pack; packed-B proposals follow because B is already loaded contiguously, so added packing may cost more than it saves. Traversal, fusion, audit, prefetch, store-form, and fallback-tail proposals have higher uncertainty or added correctness risk; address_generation's output-store writeback needs assembler confirmation. Historical K-loop attempts did not promote, and their noisy scores do not establish causes. All proposals are unverified; this order is advice, not measured evidence.
